<description>
Add a new index `txoscriptindex` which indexes all output scripts. Introduce a new `getscripthistory` RPC that returns all transactions that create outputs corresponding to the provided scripts, and optionally the transactions that spend those outputs if `txospenderindex` is also configured.

This has been a long-requested feature, attempted in previous PRs (#2802, #3652, #6835, #10370, #14053).
Some concerns raised were about the ability for an index like this to scale. I think the new techniques being used to build the indexes (https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/pull/35531, https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/pull/36002) alleviate this concern. This index can be synced in a few hours and the current disk usage is ~54 GB. This is less than the ~66 GB `txindex` disk usage in v31 and earlier. This index can also be used with a pruned node, so a full node can be supported in < 100 GB of disk space. Missing blocks are returned by hash and can be requested from peers using `getblockfrompeer`.

Some other previous concerns were more conceptual, that this type of index could encourage address reuse and chain analysis. IMO this ship has sailed, and the current status quo of not shipping an address index is turning off users who expect this functionality. Workarounds involve installing, configuring, and syncing other third-party software, making the UX of using Bitcoin Core in a self-sovereign way unnecessarily difficult.

The index hashes each output script with SHA256, then applies salted SipHash-1-3-UJ and stores a six-byte prefix. This is to support the popular Electrum protocol, which supplies only the script hash. The RPC can also look up by address or descriptors. Ranged descriptors are also supported, so a single RPC call can return the entire history of a receive/change xpub pair.

Because there are some scripts with millions of outputs, we introduce a new `OrderedVarInt` which serializes the block height after the script hash prefix. This lets LevelDB seek directly to the prefix + block height, so we can page by block height range.

To prevent DoS concerns by supplying an address with millions of outputs, the RPC tracks a byte budget of reads and throws immediately if too many reads are attempted. The error message instructs the user to narrow the block range.

Improvements to `txospenderindex` (https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/pull/36480) will also allow us to use that pruned. The end result would allow users to run with all optional indexes (including this one) in < 200 GB of disk space. Of course a larger pruned setting would be desired if many historical block lookups were being requested.
</description>

[2026-11-25] c:7161835988 comment by jaromil (contributor):
I did some quick tests locally, and I think there’s a spentness bug when two coinbases have the same txid. What made me look twice was that changing only `start_height` changed the reported spender for the same output.

I used regtest with `-testactivationheight=bip34@2`. That let me use the height-102 encoding in the coinbase at height 1, before BIP34 activated. I spent its output at height 101, then mined the identical coinbase at height 102. BIP30 permits reusing the txid once all outputs of the earlier transaction have been spent. At tip 102, `gettxout` showed the new output with one confirmation, as expected.

Here’s what `getscripthistory` returned for output 0, with the mempool excluded throughout.

| Query at tip 102 | Expected | Observed |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Live, both occurrences | Height 1 spent, height 102 unspent | Both unspent |
| `asof` set to the tip hash, both occurrences | Height 1 spent, height 102 unspent | Height 1 spent, height 102 unspent |
| Same `asof`, with `start_height=102` | Height 102 unspent | Spent by the transaction at height 101 |

The live path checks whether the outpoint exists in the current UTXO set. Both coinbases have the same txid and output number, so the coin created at height 102 makes both occurrences look unspent. I think comparing the coin’s creation height with the height of the match would fix that part.

For historical queries, the unresolved outputs are also keyed by outpoint. With both coinbases in the result, the height-101 spend gets associated with the first one. When I ask for just height 102, the same spend gets associated with the second one. The code checks that the spender is on the chain through `asof`, but it never checks whether the output had been created by the time of the spend.

I think the creation position needs to be carried through spender resolution. `FindSpender` currently returns the first spend it finds for an outpoint. If the later coinbase is eventually spent too, the lookup needs to keep looking past the earlier spend. I’d keep the full-history and single-page queries together in a regression test, since the full historical query on its own gives the expected answer.

I also noticed a separate issue with mempool locking. With `include_mempool=true` and no `end_height`, the RPC holds `pool->cs` while it sorts the entire mempool and scans every output, even for an address with no matches. I haven’t measured how long that holds the lock on a busy node, but transaction admission can wait behind it. Could we scan transaction references outside the lock and sort just the matches?
</new_statements>
